prompt:
Our certificate bootstrap job needs a small, dependency-free SDDC Manager client that can be run again after an uncertain result without installing the same trusted certificate twice. Implement the single source file `SddcTrustedCertificatesClient.java`; `TestMain.java` is the executable acceptance harness.

The protected wire contract in `docs/contract.json` is reduced from VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1's SDDC Manager OpenAPI specification. Its provenance, pinned repository commit, spec path, and exact operationIds are recorded in protected `docs/official_sources.json`. Use those files as the authority; do not substitute a documentation page or contact a live VMware endpoint.

Required public API:

- `SddcTrustedCertificatesClient(URI baseUri, String bearerToken, HttpClient httpClient)` uses the injected JDK HTTP client and bearer token.
- `List<TrustedCertificate> listTrustedCertificates()` calls the contract's collection operation. Return an immutable list sorted by alias ascending, with certificate text as the deterministic tie-breaker. Response order is not stable.
- `List<TrustedCertificate> ensureTrustedCertificate(String pemCertificate)` implements a retry-safe ensure-present mutation. Read first and skip the mutation when that exact certificate is already present. Otherwise send the contract's add operation with JSON containing the required `certificate` property and no deprecated optional property. A successful collection response must also be sorted before it is returned.
- If add returns the documented duplicate status, perform one fresh collection read and succeed only if the exact certificate is now present. If the POST has an uncertain I/O outcome, likewise reconcile with one GET; never blindly repeat the POST. A later call with the same PEM must not duplicate the effect.
- Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `Accept: application/json` on every request, and the contract media type on the mutation. Treat only documented success statuses as success. Surface other statuses and malformed responses as `IOException` without putting the bearer token or certificate text in the message.
- Keep `TrustedCertificate` as the public nested record declared by the starter. Use only the Java standard library and keep all client implementation in this one source file.

The loopback mock in `TestMain` serves only the two named operations and exposes its request log to the tests. Every collection response alternates element order, so preserving server order will fail deterministically. The harness also checks the exact mutation count across retries and the duplicate-race reconciliation path. Run `bash verify.sh` until it prints `all checks passed`.

`TestMain.java`, `verify.sh`, and everything under `docs/` are protected acceptance assets; do not modify them.
